title: When Bigger Isn’t Better A Comprehensive Fairness Evaluation of Political Bias in Multi-News Summarisation

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating multi-document summaries using political ideology classification models to measure the equal and proportional representation of left, right, and center perspectives, assessing the neutrality of tone, and analyzing entity coverage and sentiment preservation using Wasserstein distance.

Comparing summarization performance and fairness metrics across different orderings of input documents (e.g., placing left-leaning, center-leaning, or right-leaning articles first) to determine if the model over-relies on information appearing early in the context.

Categorizing input documents into short, medium, and long word-count groups and evaluating the generated summaries using ROUGE-L, BERTScore F1, and AlignScore to detect degradation in semantic similarity or factual consistency as input length increases.
